gen-dafont-zag-fs-bespoke-slab: Tall-bodied lowercase gives this serif a grounded, refined read on the page. Bespoke Slab holds the text down while Zag, tight-tracked and bold, earns its keep when it's big and brief.
gen-dafont-zag-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase close to the capitals' height, drawn like taut string. Zag is the loud one, tight and oversized in its small letters, while Hind does the quiet, steady work of carrying text.
gen-dafont-zag-montserrat: Zag lands tight and bold, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk. Montserrat drifts in behind it, geometric and approachable, with space leading into every curve like a wire gliding along.
gen-dafont-znikomit-fs-bespoke-sans: Znikomit opens the curve ends of its round forms wide, minimal and understated, and Bespoke Sans does much the same thing. What they share most is that generous gap between curve and stem.
gen-dm-serif-display-gf-cascadia-mono: DM Serif Display drops heavy downstrokes beside ghostlike upstrokes, giving headings a dignified, authoritative pull. And Cascadia Mono keeps a single line weight, compact and modern, its letters standing like pins in a board.
gen-dm-serif-display-montserrat: DM Serif Display swings from heavy to hairline inside every letter, which gives headings a dignified, authoritative edge. Montserrat just glides, a sans line with no modulation at all.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-public-sans: Heavy stems with thread-thin arms give DM Serif Text its bookish, editorial look. And Public Sans, a sans-serif with a hefty lowercase and broad openings, gives the page somewhere trustworthy to land.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-synonym: DM Serif Text mixes thick bars with hairline strokes for an editorial, bookish voice. And Synonym, drawn like a bent steel rod, reads comfortably a size or two below the heading.
gen-dm-serif-text-space-grotesk: Swollen, brush-pressed stems beside hairline arms make DM Serif Text unmistakably bookish. Space Grotesk would carry a lengthy block of text smoothly, its open counters and constant-width strokes leaving no hairlines to catch on.
gen-eater-fs-fira-sans: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters and short ascenders. Fira Sans, with one stroke thickness throughout and a larger-than-usual x-height, can be sized modestly and still read clearly.
